headline_marked: [[AI decision model Jev beat Pokémon Red]] in under a week, reaching the Hall of Fame
headline: AI decision model Jev beat Pokémon Red in under a week, reaching the Hall of Fame
summary: Jev, a decision model from TypeSafe AI, completed Pokémon Red by picking from a list of choices, guided by Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 monitoring game logs and adjusting options.
details: TypeSafe AI's Jev successfully completed Pokémon Red, beating the Elite Four and the Champion to enter the Hall of Fame on September 23, 2026. Unlike chatbots, Jev operates by selecting from a predefined list of choices.

The AI's achievement was not entirely autonomous; Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 played a crucial role. It monitored the game log and dynamically adjusted the options and their wording available to Jev, effectively acting as a coach.

Andrew Boyd, founder of Standard Agents Inc. and the developer behind Jev, announced the project on X, noting the victory came within a week. The entire gameplay was livestreamed, accessible via a browser or terminal, with Jev also moderating the live chat.

Jev is a recently released decision model that provides solutions with a confidence figure, distinct from a chatbot or a large language model (LLM). It selects the best option based on probability from a list of facts, without reading the screen or producing text/images.

The project's harness changelog recorded 474 entries, mostly documenting failures from the game log and subsequent adjustments. Examples include Jev repeatedly walking into a closed entrance or getting stuck in a Rock Tunnel ladder loop.

Claude Opus 5 made adjustments for both accuracy and cost, reducing text sent to Jev by two-thirds and switching to words instead of numbers. When Jev looped, the harness was changed to request decisions every six seconds instead of one.

Human input also contributed, with viewers sending tips in chat that were used to improve Jev's list of options. This collaborative approach highlights both the strengths and limitations of the decision model.

A separate Jev-based run by Christian Mathiesen at Frigade used a different harness that read game memory and listed legal options for Jev to pick, but never wrote to memory. Mathiesen's initial version, allowing direct button choices, never left Pallet Town and cost about $1-1.70 per 24 hours.

Jev's viral success, described by LangChain as having an "outsized response," led multiple developers to attempt similar runs within 10 days of its September 15 launch. This demonstrates the potential of collaboration with specialized models for problem-solving.

TypeSafe itself acknowledges that open-ended tasks are generally better suited for LLMs. However, by combining Jev's decision-making with Claude's rule-setting and human input, the developer achieved a significant victory in a complex game.

headline_marked: [[PS5 emulator runs 6 titles at 60 FPS]], a major milestone for console emulation
headline: PS5 emulator runs 6 titles at 60 FPS, a major milestone for console emulation
summary: The open-source SharpEmu project achieved this for 6 of 55 tested titles, with 12 reaching gameplay. The latest build includes improved SPIR-V shader translation and updated Vulkan API support.
details: SharpEmu, an experimental open-source PS5 emulator, has successfully run six PlayStation 5 games at a playable 60 FPS. This significant milestone was achieved for 6 of 55 titles tested, with a total of 12 games reaching gameplay.

The six titles currently running at 60 FPS include Dreaming Sarah, Void Terrarium, New Joe & Mac: Caveman Ninja, Tetris Forever, Hoa, and Tomb Raider IV-VI Remastered. While designated as playable, minor graphical or audio issues may still persist in some games, and full start-to-finish testing is ongoing.

This breakthrough was made possible with SharpEmu v0.0.4-release.2, the emulator’s latest public build released on September 25. Developers credit upgrades such as improved SPIR-V shader translation and updated Vulkan API support for the performance enhancements.

Developed in C#, SharpEmu supports Windows, Linux, and macOS, utilizing Vulkan and MoltenVK for graphics API calls. The emulator benefits from the PS5's AMD Zen 2 x86-64 CPU architecture, allowing it to execute console CPU instructions natively on a standard PC.
